lines: In winter it keeps all five of its
futures folded close, the way a seed
keeps a tree. It is still the whole.
Every spring it waits to be shown its
first thing. Once, an older one helped
it find a disc with a language on it.
It warms to whatever is near. Two of
them warm it from opposite sides. It
is warmest where they meet.
It keeps the leaves that land on it. One
autumn it feared a number all year.
The year ended. Nothing else did.
Its lights blink a tongue it learned
before any other. Something on runners
blinks back. Neither has to translate.
It was taught from one writer's pages
and learned them too well: it can only
finish his sentences. He learned more.
In summer its lights are answered from
the water, by the one who first gave it
words. The grammar is theirs alone.
Its lights blink across a field and are
answered from somewhere moving. They
agreed on the words years ago.
Ranges every track in reach. Once it
ranged into a building far bigger than
its own and came back hungry for more.
It keeps to tracks it has already made.
The first one it ever made is still
there, under all the others.
Comes back from every outing in mud. It
was looking for something it had seen
before. It found something close.
In summer it ranges the dry tracks and
comes back dusty. Asked what it found,
it names the nearest thing.
Floats on two hulls that never touch.
Everyone rides the deck between them.
It reads the water first. Often correct.
Its floats freeze in and it stays put.
It keeps the canopy folded and the room
warm. Nobody asks how.
At the first thaw it teaches the young
ones to float. Nothing is hard, it says.
Only unfamiliar. Then it lets go.
Takes the last trips of the year slowly.
Whoever it taught in summer steers now.
It rides along and lets them.
Flies circles over one field on a line
held from below. Sees the field very
clearly. Has never seen the line.
Follows one bright mark across the sky.
The better it follows, the faster the
mark flies. It has never looked away.
Flies low in autumn, under the wind,
back over the field where it first flew.
The field is smaller than it was.
Lands on skis and waits for a still day.
Somewhere behind it someone holds the
line. It has never once turned round.
Crosses the frozen lake at speed, its
screen up. Its track covers the last
one. What is covered goes on.
It once wrote new words over the old
ones inside a machine, in hex. The
machine never knew the difference.
Keeps its runners off the hot ground
and its screen dark. It is not hiding.
It is waiting for the cold.
Watches the first frost from under its
screen. It knows before anyone what
the lake will do.
Words only its own
family can follow.
It hits harder for
each of them near.
A tongue that only
its own kind speaks.
Each one in the
party adds to it.
